title: He Sang to Her Every Day for Two Years — Now Aamir Khan Is Getting Married Again
excerpt: The 61-year-old superstar will marry Gauri Spratt on July 5 in a private Mumbai ceremony, capping a love story that began as a friendship 25 years ago and survived two decades of silence.
body:
Six days from now, on a quiet Saturday in Mumbai, Aamir Khan will get married for the third time.

No mandap the size of a film set. No guest list that reads like a Filmfare invite. No paparazzi wall. Just a private signing at home, a handful of family, and the woman he says has made him feel complete — Gauri Spratt, a Bengaluru-born fashion and wellness entrepreneur who, by all accounts, is the most un-Bollywood partner Mr. Perfectionist has ever chosen.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=-mauwyqcE9g

The actor confirmed the July 5 date himself, telling *Variety India* with characteristic directness: "The news about the marriage is true. It's on 5 July." No spin. No publicist buffer. Just Aamir being Aamir.

A 25-Year Friendship That Became Everything

Here's the part that makes this story more interesting than your standard Bollywood wedding announcement: Aamir and Gauri first met nearly 25 years ago, long before she became a fixture at his screenings and long before he became the kind of star who could make a nation weep with a cricket match in *Lagaan*.

They lost touch. Life happened — marriages, children, careers on different continents. Aamir married Reena Dutta in 1986, had two children (Junaid and Ira Khan), and divorced in 2002. He then married filmmaker Kiran Rao in 2005; their son Azad arrived via surrogacy in 2011. That marriage ended in 2021, though the two remain close collaborators and co-parents.

Gauri, meanwhile, built her own life. Half-Tamilian, half-Irish, she studied at the University of the Arts London, ran BBlunt Salon in Mumbai, and was raising a young son from a previous marriage. Sometime around 2024, Aamir's cousin Nuzhat Khan reconnected the two in Bengaluru. What started as catching up over old memories turned into something neither of them had planned.

> "Gauri and I met 25 years ago, and now we are partners. We are very serious and committed to each other. I sing to her every day." — Aamir Khan, at his 60th birthday celebration

By March 2025, Aamir had done something genuinely surprising for a man who once kept his personal life locked tighter than a Yash Raj script vault: he introduced Gauri to the press at his 60th birthday bash. He even dropped a *Lagaan* callback — *"Bhuvan ko uski Gauri mil hi gayi"* — and the room melted.

The Quiet Domestic Life Nobody Expected

For over a year before the wedding announcement, Aamir and Gauri had already been living together. Sources describe a household that is warm, blended, and deliberately low-key — Aamir's children, Gauri's son, family dinners, a life that looks nothing like the tabloid version of a Bollywood superstar's existence.

In an interview with *Navbharat Times* this April, Aamir opened up with a vulnerability that felt earned rather than performed:

> "I am very fortunate that I met Gauri. She is great, I feel at peace with her. Although my relationship with Kiran Rao and Reena Dutta was also very deep, things didn't work out. Mujhe lagta hai ab jaake mai mukammal hua hu." — *I feel complete today.*

That last line — *mukammal* — landed differently than most celebrity soundbites. This wasn't a press tour. It was a man at 61 acknowledging that he'd finally found the thing he'd been circling for decades.

Why This Matters for the Diaspora

For millions of NRI families, Aamir Khan isn't just a movie star — he's the guy who made your parents cry during *Taare Zameen Par*, the reason your uncle won't stop quoting *3 Idiots*, the actor who turned *Dangal* into a global phenomenon that played as well in Beijing as it did in Bihar. His personal life has always been held to a different standard, partly because he's never hidden behind the usual Bollywood deflections.

A third marriage at 61, to a woman outside the industry, with no spectacle attached — it's quietly radical for a culture that still whispers about divorce and raises eyebrows at unconventional timelines. Aamir choosing to formalise his relationship with Gauri in the most private way possible says something about where he is now: done performing, interested only in what's real.

What Comes Next

Professionally, Aamir has been largely off-screen since the mixed reception of *Laal Singh Chaddha* in 2022, though industry whispers suggest he has at least two projects in various stages of development. For now, though, the headlines belong to his personal life — and for once, the story is gentle.

The ceremony on July 5 will reportedly be a registered marriage with immediate family only. No elaborate *baraat*. No five-day celebration. Just two people who found each other twice across a quarter-century, deciding it was finally time to make it official.

Sometimes the best love stories don't need a trailer.
